name.name: BSP_World_ReleaseExpiredObjects
name.evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc_fixed_step, read-only analysis. __thiscall void(world), RET at 0090366c, body 00903610-0090366c. Caller 00875bb0 at 00875eda with ECX=[[00e188a8]+19cch], the world object; also 00874d00. Walks the list at [[this+4h]] through +38h: a node whose counter +6ch is at least 1 is incremented, and once it reaches 3 the node sub-list at +50h is drained through 009035e0 and the node destroyed through vtable[0](1), with the walk resuming from the predecessor. Objects are therefore released two fixed steps after they are marked. docs/FIXED_STEP_FANOUT.md | Packet cc2_entity_event_queues: the counter at +6Ch is set to 1 by 00922FD0 and aged once per pass, so an entity is released on the second pass after marking (1 to 2 to 3). A counter of zero or less is skipped by the signed test at 00903625 and never becomes the resume anchor, which is why after a release the walk resumes at the last aged entity and re-examines the unmarked ones in between. The chain is the world node's child list, [[world+4h]] through +38h, the one 00904BF0 walks.
